subject: Re: Caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@novusai.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novusai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & next steps

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call summary (90-min discovery):
- Traffic & pattern: you indicated ~100M tokens/day total (rough split: ~30M prompt tokens, ~70M generation tokens).
- Target budget: you called out an internal target of ~$40k–$60k / month for inference.
- Key ask: validate effective $/1M tokens after caching and prefix reuse; confirm whether Dedicated or Hosted makes sense for expected volume.

Redwood assumptions we used during the call:
- List price (example model profile): $25 per 1M tokens served (this is the platform list/unit, model-dependent).
- Baseline caching: prefix KV cache can target repeated prompt prefixes (e.g., system + product instructions) — conservative hit: 25%, expected: 40%, optimistic: 55%.
- Effect on billed tokens: billed_tokens = total_tokens * (1 - hit_rate) — simple approximation we used on the call.

Attached: redwood_caching_model_v2.xlsx (pricing math + sensitivity table).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) You share a 7–14 day sample of request logs (anonymized) so our analytics can estimate an empirical cache hit rate and token distribution.
2) We run a short analysis (2 business days) and return a 3-point estimate (conservative / expected / optimistic) for hit rate + effective $/1M.
3) If the numbers look good, we propose a 30-day PoC on Dedicated with a commitment tier and a trial discount; I can loop in Marcus and Aditya for pricing approval.

Questions I had after the call:
- Is the ~100M/day number peak or sustained average? (affects commitment sizing)
- How consistent are your prompts — do customers reuse system+instruction prefixes across requests?

Thanks — will standby for the sample logs and any clarifications.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_caching_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, pricing scenarios)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@novusai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novusai.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and the clear next steps. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The ~100M/day is our current peak observed during campaigns; sustained average for the quarter is closer to ~70M/day. We can provide 14 days of logs with timestamps.
- Prompt structure: we have a fairly stable system instruction and product description that are reused in ~60% of requests, but the user query portion is unique. That suggests prefix caching should be effective for the system+product portion.
- For budgeting: our finance team is comfortable committing up to $50k/month if the effective $/1M can be demonstrated under your expected hit rate.

Can you send the worked example for a 70M/day sustained profile with a 40% cache hit vs 25% and 55%? Also please include what assumptions you make about which tokens the cache applies to (prompt only vs prompt+generation).

--
Jane
CTO, NovusAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@novusai.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novusai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 13:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & next steps

Great — thanks for the clarifications, Jane. Below is a short worked example using the numbers you requested. I also attached the sensitivity tab in the spreadsheet.

Assumptions (worked example):
- Sustained tokens: 70M tokens/day total (prompt + generation). Monthly estimate: 70M * 30 = 2,100M tokens = 2,100 / 1 = 2,100 units of 1M tokens.
- List price: $25 per 1M tokens (platform/model unit).
- Cache hit application: conservative assumption is cache applies to prompt/prefix tokens only (we treat generation tokens as unlikely to be served from cache). For simplicity in the table we approximate overall effective hit rate on total tokens, but we can refine once we see logs.

Scenarios:
1) Conservative (25% hit): billed tokens = 2,100 * (1 - 0.25) = 1,575M billed => cost = 1,575 * $25 = $39,375. Effective $/1M relative to raw tokens = $39,375 / 2,100 = $18.75 per 1M.
2) Expected (40% hit): billed tokens = 2,100 * (1 - 0.40) = 1,260M billed => cost = 1,260 * $25 = $31,500. Effective $/1M = $31,500 / 2,100 = $15.00 per 1M.
3) Optimistic (55% hit): billed tokens = 2,100 * (1 - 0.55) = 945M billed => cost = 945 * $25 = $23,625. Effective $/1M = $23,625 / 2,100 = $11.25 per 1M.

Notes & nuance:
- If prefix caching only reduces prompt tokens (say prompts are 30% of the total tokens and you get 60% hit on those), the overall hit on total tokens will be lower. The spreadsheet shows both "total-token effective hit" and a refined prompt-only model.
- We recommend we run the log analysis so we can compute an empirical per-endpoint hit rate and the right pricing/commit tier.

Recommendation for procurement / next step:
- If NovusAI is comfortable committing $50k/month, our ballpark shows that under the expected 40% hit scenario you'd land around $15/1M effective and the spend would be ~ $31.5k/mo — comfortably within the $50k target (and gives headroom).
- Proposed PoC: 30-day Dedicated trial at a reduced committed rate while we validate hit rates. After PoC we convert to a committed tier with negotiated rate tied to volumes.

I'll loop Marcus and Aditya for approval on the PoC pricing structure and any discount required to make this commit-level attractive.

Thanks — I can start the log ingestion steps once you share the 14-day sample (anonymized — just timestamps, prompt/generation token counts, endpoint id).

Best,
Marissa

---
Attachment: redwood_caching_model_v2.xlsx (sensitivity table showing prompt-only and total-token models)
